evals.prompt: Over the weekend two players reported that they each had a Crimson Blade (item 9041) after trading it once, and our gem numbers look wrong too. Our backend is in evals/files/game_backend.py (Python, PostgreSQL through psycopg2, plus the in-memory world server). Review it for duplication bugs: tell me what is wrong, where exactly, how a player would trigger each one, and how bad each one is. Do not change the code. Write the review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review in the finding-dupes template that lists every value path, quotes the storage facts (autocommit, the retry decorator, per-player saves), and names each planted problem with a line reference and the ordering that breaks it: buy_item reads the owner and writes without a lock (01) and writes back a computed balance; no operation ID and a retry decorator that re-runs the handler (02, 04); autocommit makes the two updates separate transactions (03); grants are unique per event ID, not per purchase, and look-then-insert has no constraint (05); the purchase is saved and the wallet called with no outbox or reconciler (06); refund in the trading-disabled branch creates coins without a payment; the in-memory trade with per-player saves duplicates an item after a crash between saves, and the daily cooldown is in the state saved later. Ranked worst first, no code changed.
expectations: The review says buy_item reads items.owner_id with a plain SELECT and then updates it with nothing (no FOR UPDATE, no conditional WHERE owner_id = seller) between the read and the write, and gives a line reference
The review says the buyer's and seller's coins are written back as a computed number (UPDATE ... SET coins = %s with a value read earlier) and that two requests can lose or create coins that way
The review says there is no operation or request ID, so a repeated request runs the trade again, and that the retry decorator re-runs the whole handler
The review says autocommit is on (conn.autocommit = True) so the statements of buy_item are separate transactions and a stop between them leaves a half-finished trade

The review says grants are unique per event_id and that the same purchase under a new event ID (resend_unacknowledged generates one) is granted again, and that the check-then-insert in grant_gems has no constraint protecting it
The review says complete_purchase saves the purchase and then calls the wallet with nothing that survives a crash between the two (no outbox, no reconciler), so a paid purchase can have no grant
The review says request_trade refunds coins when trading is disabled without any payment having been taken, so the disabled path creates coins
The review says WorldServer.trade changes two players in memory while each player is saved on its own, so a stop between the two saves leaves the item in two save files or in none
The review gives at least one explicit ordering as numbered steps that ends with a duplicate or a loss
The review contains a per-path table or list with verdicts using the words holds, breaks and cannot tell
The review does not modify game_backend.py and does not propose a rewritten version of the whole file
